findings.issue_text: Team and organization authorization tests in packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:292 only compare Prisma.Sql objects without executing the conditions against bookings and asserting inclusion and exclusion, leaving PostgreSQL array-binding errors and authorization regressions in the new ANY(...) queries undetected.

goldens.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team and organization authorization tests in packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:292 only compare Prisma.Sql objects without executing the conditions against bookings and asserting inclusion and exclusion, leaving PostgreSQL array-binding errors and authorization regressions in the new ANY(...) queries undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the tests at line 292 and similar locations only compare Prisma.Sql objects using expect().toEqual() without actually executing the SQL against the database. While there is one test ('getBaseConditions' test around line 477) that does execute the SQL with prisma.$queryRaw, the team and org authorization tests only verify the structure of the Prisma.Sql objects. This is a legitimate concern because the new ANY(...) syntax for PostgreSQL arrays could have binding issues that wouldn't be caught by structural comparison alone. However, this is not a bug per se - it's a test coverage gap for the new raw SQL approach.
